# uptrace_slo_monitor (Resource)

Manages an Uptrace SLO monitor: it tracks the share of good events against a target and alerts on its rules, such as a burn rate.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A 99.9% success SLO over 30 days, alerting on a fast burn.
resource "uptrace_slo_monitor" "example" {
  project_id = uptrace_project.example.id
  name       = "Span success SLO"

  params = {
    metrics        = [{ name = "uptrace_tracing_spans", alias = "$spans" }]
    good_query     = "histogram_count($spans{_status_code=\"ok\"})"
    total_query    = "histogram_count($spans)"
    resolution     = "1m"
    target         = 0.999
    window_kind    = "rolling"
    rolling_window = "30d"

    rules = [{
      name         = "fast burn"
      priority     = "high"
      type         = "burn_rate"
      long_window  = "1h"
      short_window = "5m"
      factor       = 14.4
    }]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Monitor name. It may hold template variables, such as {{ .Attrs.host_name }}.
- `params` (Attributes) The SLI, the target and the alert rules. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params))
- `project_id` (String) Project ID this monitor belongs to. Changing this forces recreation.

### Optional

- `channel_ids` (Set of String) Notification channel IDs, such as uptrace_telegram_channel.id. Omit to leave the links alone, as when channels name the monitor in their monitor_ids; set [] to detach every channel.
- `description` (String) Alert description sent with each notification. It may hold template variables.
- `repeat_interval` (Attributes) How often a firing alert notifies again. Omit for the server's default strategy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--repeat_interval))
- `trend_agg_func` (String) How a series' points combine into the trend an alert shows. Omit for the server default.
- `trend_sensitivity` (String) How much a value must move before the alert trend reports it. Omit for the server default.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Monitor ID.
- `status` (String) Runtime status: active, paused, firing, no_data, warming_up or disabled.

<a id="nestedatt--params"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params`

Required:

- `good_query` (String) Selector that counts good events, such as histogram_count($spans{_status_code="ok"}).
- `metrics` (Attributes List) Metrics the query refers to, each under an alias such as $requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params--metrics))
- `resolution` (String) Width of one evaluated point, such as 1m.
- `target` (Number) The good share the SLO promises, such as 0.999.
- `total_query` (String) Selector that counts every event, such as histogram_count($spans).

Optional:

- `grouping` (List of String) Expressions that split the SLO into one per group, such as service_name.
- `rolling_window` (String) Length of a rolling budget window, such as 30d. A duration string: ms, s, m, h, d (day) or w (week).
- `rules` (Attributes List) Alert rules. Omit for none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--params--rules))
- `window_kind` (String) The budget window. Omit for the server default.

<a id="nestedatt--params--metrics"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params.metrics`

Required:

- `alias` (String) Alias the query uses: $ followed by an identifier.
- `name` (String) Metric name.


<a id="nestedatt--params--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `params.rules`

Required:

- `name` (String) Rule name.
- `priority` (String) Priority of the alerts the rule opens: info, low, medium or high.
- `type` (String) burn_rate or budget_consumed.

Optional:

- `consumed_bound` (Number) budget_consumed: the consumed budget share that fires.
- `factor` (Number) burn_rate: the burn rate that fires.
- `long_window` (String) burn_rate: the long window. A duration string: ms, s, m, h, d (day) or w (week).
- `min_total` (Number) Fewest events a window needs before the rule is judged.
- `short_window` (String) burn_rate: the short window. A duration string: ms, s, m, h, d (day) or w (week).



<a id="nestedatt--repeat_interval"></a>
### Nested Schema for `repeat_interval`

Required:

- `strategy` (String) default, fixed (every interval), linear or exponential (from min up to max).

Optional:

- `interval` (String) Repeat interval of the fixed strategy. A duration string: ms, s, m, h, d (day) or w (week).
- `max` (String) Last interval of the linear and exponential strategies. A duration string: ms, s, m, h, d (day) or w (week).
- `min` (String) First interval of the linear and exponential strategies. A duration string: ms, s, m, h, d (day) or w (week).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a slo monitor by "<project_id>:<monitor_id>".
terraform import uptrace_slo_monitor.example 456:789
```
